title: Emergency contraception
what: This is a way to prevent pregnancy after unprotected sex. It is usually a pill. Sometimes the doctor places an IUD.
why: If you had unprotected sex, a condom broke, or you missed birth control pills.
duration: the sooner, the better: usually within the first 72 hours, some methods up to 5 days
tell_doctor: When you had sex: the exact time
If you took emergency contraception recently

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Do not wait. The sooner you act, the better it works.

prepare.title: Advice
prepare.text: See a doctor or go to a clinic. They will tell you which method is right for you.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: The pill is usually taken after a light meal, so you feel less sick.

bring: The date of your last period
steps: You tell the doctor when you had sex
The doctor asks about your cycle and health
You take the pill with the doctor or at home
If an IUD is chosen, it is placed on the exam chair
The doctor explains what to do next
feel: Your next period may come earlier or later
after: If you vomit within 2 to 3 hours of taking the pill, call your doctor
If your period is more than a week late, take a pregnancy test
Talk with your doctor about regular birth control
Get tested for infections if you were with a new partner
red_flags: Severe pain low in your belly, especially on one side: call emergency services
Fainting or severe weakness: call emergency services

faq.a: No. Emergency contraception prevents pregnancy. It does not end one.
No, it is a backup. For regular protection, choose a method with your doctor.

reminders.text: Do not wait: the sooner you take emergency contraception, the better it works.
